overall: The AG found the Holyoke City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an executive session notice for a February 6 litigation discussion that did not identify the litigation matter, and ordered announcement of the matter and release of minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Feb. 6 executive session notice was insufficient because it said only 'Litigation Update' and did not identify the litigation matter to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify the litigation matter to be discussed in executive session on February 6.

allegations.summary: The AG noted the executive session notice was found only on the city website, but the complaint did not allege improper posting, so the AG did not address it.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint does not allege that the notice was improperly posted, only that it was insufficient, we do not address this issue.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Announce at the Council's next open session meeting the specific litigation matter discussed in executive session on February 6.
Release the February 6 executive session minutes to the public within 30 days of the letter and certify to the AG that it has done so.
The Council may not rely on the Open Meeting Law as the basis for continuing to withhold the February 6 minutes (privilege or Public Records Law exemptions may still apply).
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
